page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.small is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance within the ecs.c1 server family, running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with a single thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is not active. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU.

This server type does not include local storage, requiring the attachment of external block storage for operating system and application data. It also lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses. An analysis of the CPU flags reveals the absence of modern instruction set extensions, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-assisted cryptography (AES, SHA_NI), which limits its efficiency for vector math, deep learning, and cryptographic operations.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.c1.small offers a compute-heavy profile relative to its memory capacity. This design makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU cores but have minimal memory requirements. Appropriate workloads include basic batch processing, legacy x86_64 applications, and distributed computing tasks that do not rely on modern instruction sets or local storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.small is an x86_64 virtual machine in the ecs.c1 family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with one thread per core, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. This configuration results in a low memory-to-CPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Furthermore, the CPU lacks modern instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512, AMX, and AES cryptographic acceleration. Qualitatively, the dedicated CPU allocation offers predictable execution for non-vectorized tasks, though the lack of hardware-accelerated cryptography and vector extensions represents a significant tradeoff for modern workloads. This server is designed for compute-focused workloads with low memory footprints, such as basic batch processing and legacy x86_64 applications that do not require advanced vector or matrix operations.
